Conference men's basketball season|2010]]) * First-team All-[[Mountain West Conference|MWC]] (2010) }} '''Darington O'Neal Hobson''' (born September 29, 1987) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player for [[Botafogo de Futebol e Regatas (basketball)|Botafogo]] of the [[Novo Basquete Brasil]]. He played college basketball for the [[New Mexico Lobos men's basketball|New Mexico Lobos]]. Born in [[Las Vegas, Nevada]], Hobson attended five high schools and a junior college before finally becoming eligible to play Division I college basketball. Hobson was drafted in the 2nd round (37th overall) of the [[2010 NBA draft]] by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]]. Hobson was waived on December 2, 2010, due to injury.[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=5877154 Bucks cut ties with Darington Hobson] ESPN.com, December 2, 2010 A year later, Hobson was re-signed by the Bucks for the [[2011–12 NBA season|2011–12 season]]. He was waived again on February 3, 2012. ==High school and junior college== Hobson attended [[Western High School (Nevada)|Western High School]] in Las Vegas for his freshmen year,{{cite web |url=http://www.golobos.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/hobson_darington00.html |title=Player Bio: Darington Hobson – NEW MEXICO OFFICIAL ATHLETIC SITE |publisher=Golobos.com |date=September 29, 1987 |access-date=March 22, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100308091159/http://www.golobos.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/hobson_darington00.html |archive-date=March 8, 2010 }} before moving to Houston, Texas to attend [[Alief Hastings High School]]. At fifteen he attended [[Leader's Academy High School for Business and Academic Success|Gulf Shores Academy]], earning his nickname of "Butta" through his pick-up play in Houston.{{cite web|last=Leung |first=Diamond |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/collegebasketballnation/post/_/id/7120/only-a-matter-of-time-for-hobson |title=Only a 'matter of time' for Hobson – College Basketball Nation Blog – ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=March 16, 2010 |access-date=March 22, 2010}} He then moved to southern California and attended his fourth high school of Calvary Baptist Christian. Eventually, he finally moved to Decatur Christian in Illinois for prep school.{{cite web|url=https://msn.foxsports.com/cbk/story/Goodman-New-Mexico-Hobson-010610# |title=Hobson making his mark after long road to New Mexico – CBK News – FOX Sports on MSN |publisher=Msn.foxsports.com |date=January 7, 2010 |access-date=March 22, 2010}} At Decatur Christian, Hobson was prompted by his coach, Alan Huss, to take the ACT, where he passed. Hobson, rated a 4-star recruit by Scout.com, was coming off a season where he averaged 19 points, 12 rebounds and 7 assists. He still needed credit, and therefore attended the [[College of Eastern Utah]], leading them to a 25–7 record where he averaged 15.2 points and 8.7 rebounds. ==College career== ===University of New Mexico=== Upon coming to UNM, Hobson broke down and cried. "You always wished that you were there and playing on that level," Hobson said. "When I finally got there, I just sat in my room and just thanked God and cried for a couple of hours because I finally got to the place where I always wanted to get." Virtually unknown coming into the season, the left-handed Hobson was the question mark in how successful UNM's season would be. The Lobos had players in Roman Martinez and [[Dairese Gary]], but the 6'7" [[point forward]] JC transfer Hobson was the key to the year where the Lobos were picked fifth in the [[Mountain West Conference]]. He did not disappoint, being the first Lobo to ever lead the team in points, rebounds and assists in the regular season. In 2010, Hobson was awarded the [[Mountain West Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year]] and Newcomer of the Year, making him the only player to ever achieve both honors in the same year.{{cite web |url=http://www.themwc.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030810aac.html |title=Mountain West Conference Announces 2009–10 Men's Basketball All-Conference Awards – MWC OFFICIAL ATHLETIC SITE |publisher=Themwc.com |date=March 8, 2010 |access-date=March 22, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111006174119/http://www.themwc.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030810aac.html |archive-date=October 6, 2011 |url-status=dead }} He was also named to First-Team All-Mountain West. He was also one of twenty-six finalists for the [[John R. Wooden Award]], which annually awards the most outstanding player in men's college basketball.{{cite web|url=http://www.woodenaward.com/?cat=3 |title=Top Candidates – Men – Wooden Award |publisher=Woodenaward.com |access-date=March 22, 2010}} On March 29, 2010, Hobson was named an Associated Press Third Team All-American, the first since [[Danny Granger]] in 2005.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=5037799 |title=Kentucky Wildcats' John Wall, DeMarcus Cousins make AP All-America team |publisher=ESPN |date=2010-03-30 |access-date=2011-03-17}} Hobson had 30 points and 10 rebounds against Louisiana Tech on November 21, 2009, going 3 for 4 from behind the arc. He had 22 points and 15 rebounds against the California on December 2, 2009, only to best that with a 29-point, 12-rebound performance against San Diego St. on February 2, including a 56-footer at the first half buzzer.{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=llvdHvVhhcM |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211215/llvdHvVhhcM |archive-date=2021-12-15 |url-status=live|title=Lobos Darrington Hobson with halftime buzzer beater |date=February 6, 2010 |publisher=YouTube |access-date=March 22, 2010}}{{cbignore}} On February 23, Hobson was two points away from being only the second Lobo in UNM history to record a triple-double, with 8 points, 10 rebounds and 11 assists. In the [[2010 Mountain West Conference men's basketball tournament]], Hobson had 28 points and 15 rebounds en route to a 75–69 Lobos victory over the Air Force Academy. {| class="wikitable" |- ! Field Goal Percentage |- | 35 | 33.6 | 15.9 | 9.3 | 4.6 | 44.0% | 36.1% |} ==Professional career== On April 13, 2010, it was reported that Hobson declared himself eligible for the NBA draft while not hiring an agent, leaving the possibility of returning to college basketball a possibility.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2010/news/story?id=5079573 |title=Sources: New Mexico Lobos' Darington Hobson declares for NBA draft but doesn't hire an agent |publisher=ESPN |date=2010-04-12 |access-date=2011-03-17}} On May 8, 2010, Hobson declared for the [[2010 NBA draft]], forfeiting his final year of eligibility at the University of New Mexico.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=5172555 |title=New Mexico's Darington Hobson elects to stay in draft |publisher=ESPN |date=2010-05-08 |access-date=2011-03-17}} On June 24, 2010, Hobson was selected with the seventh pick of the second round (37th overall) by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]]. On September 3, 2010, Hobson signed with the Bucks. After not playing during the preseason or during the regular season, he was waived on December 2, 2010, due to injury. He later re-signed with the Bucks for the 2011–12 season, but in February 2012, he was waived again. On January 1, 2013, Hobson was acquired by the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] of the [[NBA D-League]].[http://www.nba.com/dleague/santacruz/warriors_claim_hobson_1113.html Santa Cruz Warriors Claim Forward Darington Hobson] On August 29, 2013, Hobson's rights were acquired by the [[Delaware 87ers]] in the 2013 NBA Development League Expansion Draft.[http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/87ers_expansion_draft_2013_08_29.html NBA Development League Announced 2013 Expansion Draft Results] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131204005548/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/87ers_expansion_draft_2013_08_29.html |date=2013-12-04 }} In September 2014, Hobson signed with [[UniCEUB/BRB]] of Brazil for the 2014–15 season.[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/135340/darington-hobson-heads-to-brazil-he-signs-with-uniceub-brasilia.html Darington Hobson heads to Brazil. He signs with Uniceub Brasilia] He left Brazil in December 2014 after appearing in just six games for UniCEUB. On January 27, 2015, he joined the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] after his rights were traded back to the team from the 87ers on January 21.{{Cite web |url=http://santacruz.dleague.nba.com/news/warriors-acquire-ronald-roberts-jr-rights-to-darington-hobson/ |title=Warriors Acquire Ronald Roberts Jr., Rights to Darington Hobson |access-date=2015-01-29 |archive-date=2015-01-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150123191137/http://santacruz.dleague.nba.com/news/warriors-acquire-ronald-roberts-jr-rights-to-darington-hobson/ |url-status=dead }} On April 26, he won the D-League championship with the Warriors.{{cite news|title=Title Wave: Santa Cruz Wins NBA D-League Championship|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20150426/FWNSCW/|access-date=April 26, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=April 26, 2015}} On November 2, 2015, Hobson was reacquired by Santa Cruz.{{cite web|url=http://santacruz.dleague.nba.com/news/santa-cruz-warriors-announce-2015-training-camp-roster/|title=Santa Cruz Warriors Announce 2015 Training Camp Roster|work=NBA.com|date=November 2, 2015|access-date=November 3, 2015|archive-date=November 14, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151114061414/http://santacruz.dleague.nba.com/news/santa-cruz-warriors-announce-2015-training-camp-roster/|url-status=dead}} On May 25, 2016, Hobson signed with [[Guangxi Rhinos]] of the Chinese [[National Basketball League (China)|NBL]].{{cite web|url=http://www.asia-basket.com/China/news/447759/Guangxi-tabs-Darington-Hobson|title=Guangxi tabs Darington Hobson|work=Asia-Basket.com|date=May 25, 2016|access-date=October 2, 2016}} Four days later, he made his debut in a 112–95 loss against Hebei Xianglan, recording 30 points, 13 rebounds, four assists and one steal in 34 minutes.{{cite web|url=http://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/China/2016/0529_15108_3515.asp|title=Regular Season Round 1: Guangxi - Hebei X. 95-112|work=Eurobasket.com|date=May 25, 2016|access-date=October 16, 2016}} On January 29, 2018, Hobson signed with [[Panionios B.C.|Panionios]] of the [[Greek Basket League]].{{cite news|title=ENAΣ ΝΒΑer ΣΤΟΝ ΠΑΝΙΩΝΙΟ BIKOΣ COLA|url=http://panioniosbc.gr/enas-nvaer-ston-panionio-bikos-cola/|access-date=January 29, 2018|work=panioniosbc.gr|date=January 29, 2018|language=el|archive-date=January 30, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180130091241/http://panioniosbc.gr/enas-nvaer-ston-panionio-bikos-cola/|url-status=dead}} On March 2, 2018, Hobson signed with [[Rethymno Cretan Kings B.C.]] of the [[Greek Basket League]].{{Cite web|url=http://rethymnobc.gr/%CF%87%CE%BF%CE%BC%CF%80%CF%83%CE%BF%CE%BD-%CE%B1%CE%BD%CF%84%CE%B9-%CE%BC%CE%BF%CF%81%CE%B9%CF%83%CE%BF%CE%BD-%CF%83%CF%84%CE%BF-%CF%81%CE%B5%CE%B8%CF%85%CE%BC%CE%BD%CE%BF-cretan-kings/|title=Rethymno Cretan Kings BC » ΧΟΜΠΣΟΝ ΑΝΤΙ ΜΟΡΙΣΟΝ ΣΤΟ ΡΕΘΥΜΝΟ CRETAN KINGS|website=rethymnobc.gr|language=en-US|access-date=2018-05-01}}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} On November 28, 2018, Hobson signed a deal with [[Auxilium Torino]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]]{{Cite web|url=https://www.pianetabasket.com/lega-a/ufficiale-a-darington-hobson-e-un-giocatore-della-fiat-torino-169229|title=UFFICIALE A - Darington Hobson è un giocatore della Fiat Torino|website=pianetabasket.com|language=it|date=28 November 2018|trans-title=Official - Darington Hobson is a player of Fiat Torino}} On December 5, 2019, Hobson signed with the [[Illawarra Hawks]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] as an injury replacement for [[Aaron Brooks (basketball)|Aaron Brooks]].{{cite web |title=Illawarra Hawks Sign Darington Hobson |url=http://www.hawks.com.au/news/article/illawarra-hawks-sign-darington-hobson |website=www.hawks.com.au |language=en |access-date=2019-12-05 |archive-date=2019-12-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191205062544/http://www.hawks.com.au/news/article/illawarra-hawks-sign-darington-hobson |url-status=dead }} He averaged 5.9 points, 4.2 rebounds and 3.9 assists per game. On October 11, 2020, Hobson signed with [[Club Atlético Peñarol (Mar del Plata)|Peñarol]] of the Argentine [[Liga Nacional de Básquet]].{{cite news |title=Darington Hobson signs with Peñarol |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/darington-hobson-signs-with-penarol/ |website=Sportando |access-date=October 11, 2020 |date=October 11, 2020}} In 2021, he signed with [[Khaneh Basketball Khuzestan|Khaneh Khuzestan]] of the Iranian league and averaged 18 points and 8.4 rebounds per game. On January 27, 2022, Hobson signed with [[Minas Tênis Clube (basketball)|Minas Tênis Clube]] of the [[Novo Basquete Brasil]].{{cite web |last1=Freire |first1=Paulo |title=Minas ink Darington Hobson, ex Khouzestan |url=https://www.asia-basket.com/Iran/news/728425/Minas-ink-Darington-Hobson,-ex-Khouzestan |website=Asiabasket |access-date=January 27, 2022 |date=January 27, 2022}} ==Career
